pages.text: $(bold)Description:$() Five OBSR specifications are available in the field, all differentiated from the same prototype. Their functions are distinct and they are not interchangeable.
pages.title: Model Overview

pages.text: $(li)$(l)OBSR-2 - Semantic Lock$(): protects recorded targets.$(br)$(li)$(l)OBSR-1 - Guided Mutation$(): changes where a drift within range goes.$(br)$(li)$(l)OBSR-Health - Bio Stabiliser$(): uses the brains of nearby creatures as its power source to stabilise every block and creature in range.

$(li)$(l)OBSR-EX - Total Stability$(): the technical achievement of the previous iteration. Fixed coverage of an extremely wide area, unaffected by stage decay.$(br)$(li)$(l)OBSR-3 - Candidate Observer$(): not a stabilisation device.
pages.title: Model Overview (cont.)

pages.text: $(bold)Stage decay:$() The intensification of defocus erodes the effectiveness of stabilisation devices.$(br2)$(li)OBSR-2's lock becomes probabilistic in the final stage - each settlement re-rolls "whether it holds";$(br)$(li)OBSR-1's completeness is halved in the final stage.
OBSR-Health and OBSR-EX are unaffected by stage decay.$(br2)The effects of multiple anchors do not stack; the nearest one is used.

$(bold)Copying loss:$() The parameters of OBSR-EX are hard-wired. Copying it is not copying a file; it is recasting.$(br2)Every recasting loses part of the classification precision:$(br)$(li)the original covers 32 blocks;$(br)$(li)a generation-1 copy loses 10, a generation-2 copy loses 30.$(br2)Nothing can be recast beyond generation 2.
A Candidate Observer built around a copy requires more training: +50 points for a generation-1 core, +150 for a generation-2 core.$(br2)There is only one original. Where it goes is your decision.
